public_rationale: Business Insider reported on December 18, 2025 that Oracle shares had fallen 46% from their September 10 high [e5]. Kiplinger's March 10, 2026 report described Oracle's decline and reported a consensus Buy recommendation among surveyed analysts [e6]. These reports concern Oracle and do not establish a durable decline across generative-AI valuations or identify the beginning of a completed sector-wide reversal [e5] [e6]. The forecast remains unresolved.
limitations: The packet lacks comparable valuation records for a consistent set of generative-AI companies.
It lacks convergent independent histories identifying the September 2025 Oracle episode and its aftermath as the beginning of a broad unwinding.
Oracle's share-price decline and analyst recommendations cannot establish the wider valuation outcome.
The forecast specifies neither a deadline nor a valuation measure.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI valuations will eventually fall, though they may rise first, and the Oracle craze of early September 2025 and what has happened since will in hindsight be seen as the beginning of the end.
conditions: valuations may go up before they fall

our_interpretation: The plain reading predicts an eventual broad unwinding of the generative-AI valuation boom, with the September 2025 Oracle episode later recognized as its beginning.
Possible interim valuation increases are a concession, not a conditional antecedent that must occur before scoring.
An Oracle-specific decline alone does not establish a broad generative-AI reversal.
No valuation basket, currency, accounting basis or required size of decline is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Broad generative-AI valuations undergo a durable decline, and independent financial histories identify the September 2025 Oracle episode and its aftermath as the beginning of that unwinding.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An established history of the completed boom and reversal identifies a materially different beginning and rejects the September 2025 Oracle episode as the start.

evidence.explanation: The report documents Oracle's decline from its September high before Marcus published the forecast. It explains the episode he referenced but cannot establish a later sector-wide outcome.

The article reports continued Oracle weakness but also a positive analyst consensus. That combination cautions against treating one company's decline as proof that investors had accepted the end of the wider boom.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable valuation records showing a durable broad decline, together with independent financial histories identifying the September 2025 Oracle episode and its aftermath as its beginning. An established history of the completed boom and reversal that identifies a materially different beginning and rejects that episode as the start would contradict the forecast.
